title: Unit – 4 : Session – 2 : SLO – 2  |  Operations on Binary Trees — Insertion and Deletion
sections: In a binary tree, each node has at most TWO children.
The first node inserted into a binary tree is called the ROOT node.
In a binary tree insertion algorithm, if a node's left child is NULL, the new node is inserted at the LEFT position.
In a level-order insertion (used for a complete binary tree), the new node is inserted at the first available position from LEFT to RIGHT.
In recursive insertion of a binary tree, the base case occurs when the current node is NULL.
Inserting into a binary tree without any specific order results in a GENERAL (unordered/random) binary tree.
In a binary tree, a node with ZERO (no) children can be deleted by simply removing the node.
A node with one child can be deleted by linking its parent directly to its CHILD.
When deleting a node with two children, the successor or predecessor must be deleted from its ORIGINAL location.
